title: Reliable personal assistant with managed ACP workers
description: Build one dependable assistant for Milad, inspired by the continuity and delegation of Dot or Grokbot. The assistant handles conversation, lookups, context selection, planning, and supervision. Existing Cursor and a confirmed OpenAI worker perform implementation work through ACP. Use Mastra and TypeScript, with plantool as the source of truth for goals, decisions, and delivery tasks. This is a proposed roadmap for review, not authorization to implement every milestone.
why: Replace fragile ad hoc calls between coding tools with one assistant that can explain what it knows, who is doing what, and what still needs attention.

acceptance.text: One conversation can delegate a bounded task and show progress, questions, cancellation, and evidence of completion
Context survives restart and remains isolated by project
Tools and skills are inspectable and follow explicit permissions
Both requested worker targets pass compatibility checks before being advertised as supported
Failures never silently become successful completion

assumptions: Single-user local-first prototype is proposed, not yet a confirmed deployment decision
Dot and Grokbot are experience references, not a requirement to clone their full feature sets
The assistant initially supervises work rather than editing code itself

skipped.monetization: This is a personal assistant experiment. Commercial pricing and billing have not been requested.
skipped.legal: Public release and distribution are outside this prototype plan. Revisit distribution, provider terms and data handling when that scope is proposed.

answered.goal: See linked goal document and top-level acceptance criteria. Milad is the initial user.
answered.platform: Person-owned decision MAST-6 defines the first surface and deployment.
answered.stack: Mastra and TypeScript are already selected by the user and initialized. Provider/runtime choices remain explicit decisions.
answered.core-features: M0-M5 describe the first release. Later candidates are separated and blocked by the pilot.
answered.accounts: Proposed single-user local application has no new product account system. Existing provider login is verified in M0. Revisit if deployment scope changes.
answered.data: Person-owned decision MAST-14 covers storage. M2 defines scope, source, correction and deletion. Provider data transfer depends on the model decision.
answered.ui-structure: The surface decision controls implementation. Minimum flow is conversation -> task progress -> approval/question -> result evidence, with inspectable context and worker state.
answered.visual: No custom visual design required for terminal prototype. If a browser or desktop surface is chosen, define its visual direction before building it. Dot/Grokbot are behavior references.
answered.quality: M5 contains deterministic failure scenarios, opt-in live provider checks and proposed ten-task pilot. No reliability claims before evidence.
answered.offline: Offline capability remains part of the supervisor-model decision. The initial external ACP workers may require network access; a fully offline product is not assumed.

outcome.summary: Roadmap MVP milestones M2-M5 done; delegation, context, tools, workers, and acceptance evidence in repo.
